newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syrian daily says U.S. envoy offering nothing new.
newsitem.headline: Syrian daily says U.S. envoy offering nothing new.

text.p: An official Syrian newspaper said on Thursday U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross was bringing nothing new with him in his latest attempt to rescue the troubled Arab-Israeli peace process.
"What is Ross going to do if he is carrying nothing new with him?" the official daily Tishreen asked in an editorial.

"We mean by the new thing a firm American position supporting the peace process. An honest position which takes into consideration the necessity of establishing a just peace and not to cover Israel's aggressive policies," Tishreen said.
"Ross is not carrying such a position," it said.

"His efforts are only aimed at calming the situation, easing tension and urging Palestinians to accept conditions of (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu without any commitment by Washington or Israel to stop settlement building and trade (occupied) land for peace," Tishreen said.
"Such calm, even if it is achieved, would be temporary because Netanyahu does not want to commit himself to the basis of the peace process," the paper said.
The paper concluded by saying "the U.S. efforts will not bear fruit because they are biased to Israel which is increasing its obstinacy day by day."
Officials said Ross arrived in the Moroccan capital Rabat late on Wednesday at the start of another attempt to get Israelis and Palestinians to resume their peace talks.
He is due to meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat who is in Rabat to attend an Arab meeting on Jerusalem.
Syria had strongly condemned Netanyahu's decision to build a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, which has sparked violence in the West Bank and Gaza.
It also denounced Netanyahu for refusing to trade occupied Arab lands for peace and said Syrian-Israeli peace talks which broke off a year ago would not resume until he changed his policy.
Syria wants Israel to withdraw fully from the Golan Heights captured by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
